kind: A pilot that decides the stack arm of full_size_best_rate_pair: plain or with the pool that lifts the ceiling, and at which rate.
why: In full_size_rate_pilot the stack is worse at 1.2e-3 than at 6e-4 (1.34753 against 1.31985 on the first 2,000,000 validation bytes), while the Transformer is better at 1.2e-3 (1.27625 against 1.28370). Its membranes saturate there. experiments/membrane_saturation.py counts the entries whose charge reached the membrane's bound, where a neuron fires its largest count whatever more it hears and learns nothing through its charge. On the first 32,768 validation bytes: fs-st12 has 2.7% of its reads' entries at the bound (9.7% at the top level) and 2.0% of its cells' (11.8% at the top level); fs-st6 has 0.3% (1.4%) and 0.8% (5.9%). The test bed at 2.4e-3 has 0.2% and 0.1%, which is why it never showed this. v15 found the same at 1e-3 and built the pool that lifts the ceiling (--pool-lifts-ceiling): the pool divides the charge before the membrane bounds it, so a neuron fires up to its largest count at every threshold and keeps learning. Continued from 15,000 updates at 1e-3 it was 0.0187 ahead at 19,500 (docs/STREAM_FORM.md). No release used it, because every release trained at 3e-4, where nothing saturates. Now that the pair trains each model at its best rate, the stack's best rate may be set by its membranes rather than by learning.

arms.fs-st6-lift: the pilot's stack (full.sh KIND stack: v16's stack with forgetting slopes, windows of 512 bytes, batch 8, 24,000 updates, warmup 1,000, cosine over the run, seed 20001, code v17l) at peak rate 6e-4 with --pool-lifts-ceiling; 34,810,900 parameters, as the plain stack

measure: as full_size_rate_pilot: experiments/eval_stream.py on the first 2,000,000 validation bytes as 16 unbroken streams after 8,192 unscored lead bytes, averaged weights, bits kept; beside it the share of entries at the membrane bound (experiments/membrane_saturation.py, first 32,768 validation bytes) and the trainer's pulses a byte
reading: If the better lifted arm scores at least 0.010 below the plain stack's best pilot score (the best of fs-st3, fs-st6 and fs-st12), the pair's stack arm trains with the lifted ceiling at that arm's rate, in both of its stages; if the plain stack did not qualify for the pair under its own rate rule, the lifted stack takes its place on the same condition. Otherwise the pair runs as recorded. Recorded either way: both scores, the saturation of each arm and the pulses a byte.
seen_before_recording: fs-st12 1.34753, fs-tf12 1.27625, fs-st6 1.31985, fs-tf6 1.28370; the 3e-4 pair still training (fs-st3 1.5367 and fs-tf3 1.5605 in windows at 10,500 and 9,000 updates); the saturation numbers above; a 4-update CPU check of the lifted recipe at 1.2e-3 (finite, 34,810,900 parameters). No lifted full-size run has trained.
